title: HBX-14 drug substance — biologics manufacturing process data (synthetic)
description: Fictional CHO fed-batch manufacturing record for HBX-14 drug substance at Helix Biologics, Building 4 (fictional site): 240 batches across three production lines and two media suppliers, January 2023 to late 2025. Each 14-day culture carries a 6-hourly sensor series, a harvest NIR spectrum and batch release testing. Designed for teaching instrument-data ingestion, multicollinearity, principal component analysis and leakage-safe model validation. No GMP or validation framework is implied.

datasets.name: BATCHES
datasets.label: Batch Record and Release Testing
datasets.description: One row per manufactured batch: line, supplier, media lot, summarised process parameters, release testing and disposition. Every summary column (TEMP_MEAN, VCD_PEAK, LACTATE_PEAK …) is computed from that batch’s sensor series, so the two datasets agree exactly and a learner who recomputes a summary gets the published number back.

columns.name: MEDIA_LOT
columns.label: Media Lot Number
columns.notes: Lots are used for 6–10 consecutive batches, so batches sharing a lot are correlated.

columns.name: OPERATOR_SHIFT
columns.label: Operating Shift
columns.notes: Included deliberately as a variable with no effect on any outcome.

columns.name: DURATION_H
columns.label: Culture Duration (h)
columns.notes: Fixed at 336 h for every batch.

columns.name: TEMP_MEAN
columns.label: Mean Temperature (°C)
columns.derivation: Mean of TEMP_C over all 57 sensor readings for the batch.

columns.name: TEMP_SD
columns.label: Temperature Deviation SD (°C)
columns.derivation: Sample SD of (TEMP_C − TEMP_SP) over all 57 sensor readings.
columns.notes: Deviation from setpoint, not raw spread: the setpoint itself steps from 36.8 °C to 33.0 °C at hour 240, so a raw SD of TEMP_C would measure that step rather than controller behaviour. This is the most direct measure of control-loop health, and it rises sharply during the LINE-B controller fault.

columns.name: PH_MEAN
columns.label: Mean pH
columns.derivation: Mean of PH over all sensor readings.

columns.name: PH_SD
columns.label: pH Deviation SD
columns.derivation: Sample SD of (PH − PH_SP) over all 57 sensor readings.
columns.notes: Deviation from setpoint, for the same reason as TEMP_SD: the pH setpoint steps from 7.00 to 6.90 at hour 120.

columns.name: DO_MEAN
columns.label: Mean Dissolved Oxygen (%)
columns.derivation: Mean of DO_PCT over all sensor readings.

columns.name: VCD_PEAK
columns.label: Peak Viable Cell Density (10⁶ cells/mL)
columns.derivation: Maximum VCD across the sensor series.

columns.name: VCD_PEAK_H
columns.label: Hour of Peak VCD
columns.derivation: ELAPSED_H at which VCD is maximal.

columns.name: GLUCOSE_MIN
columns.label: Minimum Glucose (g/L)
columns.derivation: Minimum GLUCOSE_G_L across the sensor series.
columns.notes: The lowest pre-feed trough. Feed control holds the culture above 0.6 g/L, so this is a measure of feed adequacy rather than of starvation.

columns.name: LACTATE_PEAK
columns.label: Peak Lactate (g/L)
columns.derivation: Maximum LACTATE_G_L across the sensor series.

columns.name: OSMOLALITY
columns.label: Harvest Osmolality (mOsm/kg)
columns.notes: Offline measurement at harvest.

columns.name: PURITY_PCT
columns.label: Purity by SEC (%)
columns.notes: Release specification: ≥ 95.0%.

columns.name: AGGREGATE_PCT
columns.label: High Molecular Weight Species (%)
columns.notes: Release specification: ≤ 3.0%.

columns.name: POTENCY_PCT
columns.label: Potency (% of reference standard)
columns.notes: Release specification: 85–115%. This is the modelling outcome, and it is a BATCH-level attribute.

columns.name: YIELD_KG
columns.label: Drug Substance Yield (kg)
columns.derivation: TITER_G_L × 1,900 L harvest volume × downstream recovery ÷ 1,000.

columns.name: DISPOSITION
columns.label: Batch Disposition
columns.derivation: Rejected when any attribute is out of specification; Investigation when all are in specification but one is close to a limit; otherwise Released.

datasets.name: SENSORS
datasets.label: Bioreactor Sensor Time Series
datasets.structure: One record per batch per 6-hour reading
datasets.description: Bioreactor sensor readings every 6 hours over the 336-hour culture, 57 readings per batch. Joining batch potency onto these rows creates the modelling table for the capstone — and the leakage trap, because a row-level random split puts readings from the same batch in both training and test.

columns.name: BATCHID
columns.label: Batch Identifier
columns.notes: Foreign key to batches. This is the grouping variable for leakage-safe cross-validation.

columns.name: TIMESTAMP
columns.label: Reading Timestamp
columns.notes: ISO 8601 to the minute, UTC.

columns.name: TEMP_C
columns.label: Temperature (°C)
columns.notes: Process value. Compare against TEMP_SP rather than against a constant.

columns.name: TEMP_SP
columns.label: Temperature Setpoint (°C)
columns.notes: 36.8 °C, shifted to 33.0 °C at hour 240. Identical for every batch.

columns.name: PH
columns.label: pH
columns.notes: Process value.

columns.name: PH_SP
columns.label: pH Setpoint
columns.notes: 7.00, lowered to 6.90 at hour 120. Identical for every batch.

columns.name: DO_SP
columns.label: Dissolved Oxygen Setpoint (%)
columns.notes: Constant at 40% for every batch and every reading.

columns.name: AGIT_SP
columns.label: Agitation Setpoint (rpm)
columns.notes: 120 rpm, stepped to 145 rpm at hour 72. Identical for every batch.

columns.name: GLUCOSE_G_L
columns.label: Glucose (g/L)
columns.notes: Sawtooth: consumed continuously, replenished by bolus feeds at hours 72, 120, 168, 216 and 264.

columns.name: LACTATE_G_L
columns.label: Lactate (g/L)
columns.notes: Accumulates during growth, then consumed after the metabolic shift near hour 144.

datasets.name: SPECTRA
datasets.label: Harvest NIR Spectra
datasets.structure: One record per batch, wide over wavelength
datasets.description: Near-infrared absorbance of the harvest pool, 1100–2300 nm in 20 nm steps (61 wavelengths). Highly collinear by construction: adjacent wavelengths correlate above 0.99, which is what makes this a genuine principal-component problem rather than a demonstration of one.

columns.name: BATCHID
columns.label: Batch Identifier
columns.notes: Foreign key to batches.

columns.name: W1100 … W2300
columns.label: NIR Absorbance at 1100–2300 nm
columns.notes: 61 columns in 20 nm steps. Each spectrum carries its own baseline offset and slope (multiplicative scatter), which dominates the raw variance — PC1 of the unpreprocessed spectra is scatter, not chemistry. Standard normal variate or SNV-plus-detrend preprocessing is needed before the protein bands near 1690 nm and 2180 nm become the leading components.
